1	# Rules: Build
2	
3	- **R-7qd.** What a page lists, and what its story says, is only what the design changes compared with the app as it is now: a redesigned page the app already has shows its differences, not the whole page.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build*
5	- **R-w3n.** A story is written only when someone asks for one; a design can be built without any.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build*
7	- **R-h8x.** The agent writes one story per page, and splits it only when the parts could ship on their own, saying why.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build/stories/:group @ split-and-writing*
9	- **R-b5k.** A story says it's out of date once the design changes after it was written, and says what changed since.
10	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build @ typical*
11	- **R-z2m.** Rewriting a story that was edited by hand asks first, because the rewrite replaces those edits.
12	- **R-u6t.** A story is kept with the design on its branch, so it's reviewed and merged with the design; a person's edits are kept the same way.
13	- **R-n4j.** A page's build session is given its stories, edits and all, and checks the build against their acceptance criteria; where a story and the design differ, the design wins.
14	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build/stories/:group*
15	- **R-c9r.** A story never repeats what's already built: no built rules, no pages the app already has, and no rule from another page's story.
16	- **R-f6w.** Approving a screen as built in a build session saves only that screen; every other screen is still checked against the design.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/sessions/:session/check/:shot*
18	- **R-q3d.** A page builds only from a design approved as it is now: one that changed since it was approved says so on Build, with no Start a build session, until it's approved again.
19	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/build @ changed-since-approved*

I've made this a rule and a design decision. I didn't change any screens, because Build already shows a page with no story the right way: "No story yet", with Write the story.

**What changes**
- **The rule:** New rule R-p4w in `RULES.md`, marked proposed: once a page is built, its stories are done. If the design later changes that page again, Build shows it with no story yet, and the page's next build session isn't given the old stories.
- **Out of date:** this label now only means the story's page hasn't been built since the story was written.
- **Writing a new story:** for a built page, Write the story starts from scratch. It won't warn that it will replace hand edits, because those edits belong to the change that's already built.
- **The old story files** stay on the branch and get merged with it, as the record of what was built, until a new story replaces them.

**How the app should do it** (recorded in `NOTES.md` for whoever builds it): when a page's build session finds the page built, Prelude marks the page's `story.json` as built, with when and which session. Prelude then treats a built story as if there were none, both on Build and in what the next build session is given.

There's a gap in the preview: none of the current states shows a page that was built and then changed again, so the rule has no shown-on yet. I can add a page like that to Typical if you'd like to see it. It would show "Last built in …" and "No story yet".
"Out of date" should be for when the unbuilt design has changed since the story was written, right?

name: Edit
text: The file C:\Users\JohnHowes\.prelude\worktrees\258e60949d\prelude-build\prelude\build\NOTES.md has been updated successfully.

Yes. "Out of date" is for a story whose change hasn't been built yet, when the design has changed since the story was written. Once the change is built, the story is done, and the page's next change starts with no story.

I've reworded that line in `NOTES.md` to say exactly that. I left the rules as they are, because together they already say it: R-b5k covers the out-of-date marker, and R-p4w covers a built page's stories.
